title: Bram and the Protocol
premise: Wren Sterling, a cargo navigator haunted by the memory-backups stored in his ship's hold, answers a distress signal broadcast in a language extinct since the Meridian Massacre — an atrocity officially erased from every archive. The signal leads him to Ilsa Vane, a survivor-archivist whose people's history was rewritten by the Concord, the trade authority that owns his debts and licenses. As Wren's own navigational logs become the only unaltered record of what happened fifteen years ago, he realizes his beloved captain was complicit, and that the backups in his hold contain the minds of massacre witnesses the Concord wants destroyed. Racing a closing jump window, Wren must choose between broadcasting the truth and losing everything he is; he transmits it, sacrificing his license and identity, and ends the book as a nameless witness carrying the survivors' memories into exile.
about_author: L. M. Eastwick is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade aboard container ships before turning to fiction. They write about people who keep records for a living and live in fear of what their records say.

chapters.title: The Hold Full of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Wren Sterling runs a routine cargo haul through contested orbits, performing his nightly ritual of checking on the memory-backups stored in his hold — backups he inherited with the ship and has never dared access. His POV establishes loneliness, debt to the Concord, and quiet dread. Emotional beat: uneasy routine masking guilt.

chapters.title: A Language With No Speakers
chapters.summary: A distress signal arrives in Ashkari, a language extinct for two centuries. Wren recognizes fragments from his grandmother's lullabies — impossible, since his family claims no Ashkari blood. He decodes coordinates against protocol. Emotional beat: fascination curdling into dread as the signal names him personally.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors in Nice Suits
chapters.summary: Concord liaison Officer Brandt boards Wren's ship for a 'routine audit,' probing why he altered course toward restricted space. Wren lies for the first time in fifteen years. Flashback hints his late captain, Odile Marchetti, once hid something similar. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: Ilsa
chapters.summary: Wren finds Ilsa Vane alive in a derelict relay station, transmitting on dead frequencies to keep her people's erased language from dying twice. She believes Wren was sent by the resistance; he insists he's just a hauler. Emotional beat: wary connection between two people who both carry things they shouldn't.

chapters.title: What the Archives Deleted
chapters.summary: Ilsa shows him proof: the Meridian Massacre killed forty thousand Ashkari, then the Concord rewrote every public record. She needs one thing she can't forge — independent navigation logs from the era. Wren realizes his ship's original logs might qualify. Emotional beat: the past becoming suddenly, dangerously real.

chapters.title: Odile's Sealed Compartment
chapters.summary: Searching his own ship, Wren finds a sealed compartment behind the backup vault containing Odile's private logs — and evidence she was present at Meridian, working for the Concord. His grief curdles into betrayal. Emotional beat: mourning someone who turns out to be a monster.

chapters.title: The Backups Wake Up
chapters.summary: Accessing the backups to cross-reference Odile's logs, Wren discovers they aren't random inheritances: they are Ashkari witnesses, smuggled out before the massacre, their memories intact. One fragment speaks to him in his grandmother's voice. Emotional beat: horror and tenderness entangled.

chapters.title: Brandt's Offer
chapters.summary: Brandt corners Wren at a Concord waystation: surrender the backups and the logs, receive full debt forgiveness and a captaincy. He reveals the Concord knows exactly what Wren carries and has been waiting for him to surface. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Running
chapters.summary: Ilsa confronts Wren about his hesitation, forcing him to admit he's known something was wrong with his inheritance for years and chose comfort over truth. Their alliance nearly shatters. Emotional beat: shame spoken aloud for the first time.

chapters.title: The Witness in the Vault
chapters.summary: Wren interfaces with the oldest backup — an Ashkari archivist named Sena — and experiences the massacre through recorded memory. He comes out shaking, unable to eat, unable to pretend anymore. Emotional beat: vicarious trauma becoming personal conviction.

chapters.title: Ghost Fleet
chapters.summary: Concord patrol ships begin shadowing them through contested orbits. Wren uses fifteen years of smuggler knowledge to run silent through a debris field, buying time but burning fuel they can't replace. Emotional beat: competence as survival, fear as focus.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Ilsa calculates the only jump window that reaches the neutral tribunal relay before the Concord seals the sector — thirty-six hours away, requiring a course through a quarantine zone. Committing means no return. Emotional beat: the point of no return made literal.

chapters.title: Quarantine
chapters.summary: Inside the quarantine zone they find Meridian itself — the planet the archives say never existed — its cities still scarred, its atmosphere still wrong. Wren walks the ground where forty thousand died. Emotional beat: grief given geography.

chapters.title: Sena's Last Request
chapters.summary: Sena asks Wren not just to transmit the evidence but to carry the witnesses' memories onward — to let them live in someone willing. Wren, terrified of losing himself, refuses. Ilsa doesn't speak to him that night. Emotional beat: cowardice wearing the mask of self-preservation.

chapters.title: Betrayal Aboard
chapters.summary: Wren discovers his engineer, Tam, has been feeding position data to Brandt in exchange for Tam's family's freedom. Instead of rage, Wren feels recognition — he almost took the same deal. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a mirror.

chapters.title: Boarding Action
chapters.summary: Brandt's marines breach the ship while it charges its jump drive. Wren fights through his own corridors, defending the vault with the desperation of a man protecting graves. Tam redeems himself buying seconds and is captured. Emotional beat: violence with something worth protecting at its center.

chapters.title: Thirty Seconds to Window
chapters.summary: Damaged and bleeding, Wren makes the jump with minutes to spare, leaving Brandt's ship crippled in the debris field. The backups' vault is breached; two witnesses are lost forever. Emotional beat: survival that tastes like failure.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Relay
chapters.summary: At the neutral relay, Ilsa prepares the broadcast while Concord lawyers arrive with injunctions and forged counter-evidence. Records alone won't be enough — the tribunal demands living testimony. Emotional beat: truth arriving to find the courtroom already rigged.

chapters.title: Who Is Willing
chapters.summary: The witnesses' memories can testify, but only through a host who accepts them fully — risking dissolution of self. Wren finally understands what Sena asked. He says yes. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into consent.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Climax: Wren hosts the witnesses before the tribunal, speaking in Ashkari and Standard simultaneously, his own identity dissolving at the edges as forty thousand voices move through him. The transmission goes out on every open channel, unstoppable now. Emotional beat: selfhood offered up as evidence.

chapters.title: After the Verdict
chapters.summary: The tribunal acknowledges the massacre; the Concord begins controlled damage limitation rather than justice. Ilsa chooses to stay and fight institutionally; Wren cannot — his license revoked, his name flagged, his mind permanently shared. Emotional beat: victory that changes nothing fast enough.

chapters.title: The Nameless Navigator
chapters.summary: Resolution: Wren takes a new name and an unregistered hauler, the surviving witnesses settled in the hold not as cargo but as crew. He navigates by stars no chart lists, carrying the dead forward. Final beat: identity as a choice renewed daily, memory as a home you build for others.
